advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `changed_range` distinguish a git-diff FAILURE (non-zero exit / error) from a genuine empty diff instead of treating both as 'nothing changed'.
evidence: ABSENCE: the function never inspects git's exit status; a non-zero `git diff` produces no stdout, so `grep -q .` returns non-zero (=='no change') exactly as a genuine no-delta would.
advisory.finding: `changed_range()` discards git stderr (`2>/dev/null`) and derives 'nothing changed' from empty `grep -q .` output, so a git diff FAILURE (transient error, or a `$mcp_deployed` ref that passes `rev-parse --verify` but that `git diff` rejects) is indistinguishable from 'no delta' and silently SKIPS the mcp deploy. The result of the check cannot be told apart from the check never having run.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the footer only advances `mcp-deployed-sha` when the mcp gate is known to have been evaluated cleanly (not fail-open-skipped), so a swallowed diff error cannot permanently mark an undeployed mcp change as deployed.
evidence: 803: # Keep mcp's marker in lockstep on a COMPLETE deploy: the mcp block may have been a no-op this
ABSENCE: the footer write assumes 'mcp block did not run' == 'mcp genuinely had no change', which the fail-open gate cannot guarantee.
advisory.finding: The footer unconditionally stamps `MCP_SHA_FILE=$TARGET` on any complete tick (line 806), even when the mcp gate was skipped. Combined with the fail-open `changed_range`, if a genuine mcp change existed but its diff errored and was treated as no-op, the tick still completes, advances mcp-deployed-sha to $TARGET, and the undeployed mcp change is PERMANENTLY lost — the next tick diffs from $TARGET and sees no delta.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test seeding an unparseable $STATE_DIR/mcp-deployed-sha (e.g. 'garbage') and assert the mcp gate falls back to $DEPLOYED as baseline.
evidence: Added source: `mcp_deployed="$(cat "$MCP_SHA_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"` then `if [ -z "$mcp_deployed" ] || ! git -C "$MIRROR_DIR" rev-parse --verify -q "$mcp_deployed^{commit}" ... ; then mcp_deployed="$DEPLOYED"; fi`
Comment claims: 'falling back to the global sha when absent or unparseable, so the first tick after this lands decides exactly as it does today.'

ABSENCE: the new tests seed either no marker (fixture default) or a valid marker written by a prior tick; none writes an unparseable value like 'garbage' into $STATE_DIR/mcp-deployed-sha to force the `! git rev-parse --verify` branch. Named violating input: `state/mcp-deployed-sha` containing `"garbage"` — the fallback must yield mcp_deployed==$DEPLOYED so the mcp gate diffs from DEPLOYED, not from the corrupt marker.
advisory.finding: The added mcp-baseline fallback branch (absent OR unparseable MCP_SHA_FILE falls back to $DEPLOYED) is untested: no new test seeds a garbage/unparseable mcp-deployed-sha and asserts the tick still decides from $DEPLOYED. The absent case is exercised implicitly (fixture starts with no marker), but the 'present but unparseable' rev-parse guard is not.
scenarios: A partial/corrupt write to mcp-deployed-sha (interrupted mv) leaves an unparseable ref; the fallback must restore today's DEPLOYED-based decision rather than mis-scoping or skipping the mcp deploy.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that writes a non-commit value to mcp-deployed-sha before _run, then asserts the mcp block decides identically to a first-tick (marker-absent) run — i.e. mcp deploys iff DEPLOYED..TARGET touches MCP_PATHS.
